newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures remained mired in a narrow range throughout Monday's session after being marked slightly lower at the open following the weaker tone in Bunds.
Traders said activity was subdued as investors remained cautious ahead of the result of the U.S. presidential election even though few were in any doubt what the outcome would be.
The other notable features were a weakening of the franc against the mark and a continuation of the outperformance by French short-dated cash bonds over their German equivalents.
The franc slipped as low as 3.3835 from the day's high of 3.3789 per mark and was at 3.3818 at 1630 GMT.

Traders said the franc came under slight pressure after European Union officials said the post-EMU budget stability pact would not be ready by the end of this year because of German insistance on tough measures.
Iain Lindsay, bond analyst at Credit Lyonnais, said so much progress had already been made on the stability pact that most people expected the final stages to be more or less a formality.

Some people also said an article in French newspaper Le Monde which reported advisers to Philippe Seguin were recommending a devaluation of the franc to boost the economy, weighed on the currency as well.
The French unit was helped off the lows after a German official said the main points of the so-called stability pact would be agreed by December and Germany wanted a solid and credible pact.
At the short end of the curve, French bonds outperformed as they lagged behind curve flattening moves seen in Germany on Monday, analysts said.
The two-year spread moved as low as 20 basis points while the five-year spread touched minus 14 basis points.
"France hasn't reacted so much to the flattening but it can't buck the trend," said Lindsay at Credit Lyonnais.
Some analysts had expected French call money, closely steered by the Bank of France, to be eased on Monday, given the cut in the intervention rate last week.
Traders said Caisse Nationale de Credit Agricole had tried to ease call money, but the French overnight rate remained unchanged at 3-1/4 3/8 percent.
